queries: gh search code 'BashOperator "dbt run" language:python' --limit 50 --json repository,path
gh search code 'KubernetesPodOperator dbt language:python' --limit 50 --json repository,path
gh search code 'DockerOperator dbt language:python' --limit 50 --json repository,path
gh search code 'DbtTaskGroup ProjectConfig language:python' --limit 30 --json repository,path
gh search code 'DbtDag ProjectConfig language:python' --limit 30 --json repository,path
shortfalls: The two Cosmos queries ran dry: across their 60 hits only one came from a repository that was not already labelled, excluded or passed over (hainguyenle89/airflow-dags, from the DbtDag query). The two missing Cosmos places went to one more repository from the BashOperator query and one more from the DockerOperator query, so the mix is 4 BashOperator, 3 KubernetesPodOperator, 4 DockerOperator and 1 Cosmos. No candidate was rejected. No link expects unknown.
selection_notes: Searches run on 2026-11-16 with the five queries above; hits were taken in returned order, none skipped for being easy or hard. Passed over without counting as rejections: the 17 first-corpus repositories and the 7 excluded ones (listed under excluded), and the six the first corpus rejected for reasons that still hold (airflow-plugins/Example-Airflow-DAGs, GoogleCloudPlatform/professional-services, UllasP0707/bellwether, gmyrianthous/dbt-airflow, awslabs/runner-dbt-aws-airflow, cal-itp/data-infra). hainguyenle89/airflow-dags, which the first corpus found qualifying but did not take, was eligible and was taken. Stopping points (1-based hit numbers in the returned order): BashOperator query after Rodrigo-Henrique21/data_pipeline_airflow_dbt (hit 17; taken hits 11, 15, 16, 17); KubernetesPodOperator query after grinfeld/py_spark_playground (hit 12; taken hits 10, 11, 12); DockerOperator query after rionurfadilah229/ELT-Pipeline (hit 8; taken hits 5, 6, 7, 8); DbtTaskGroup query read to its end (30 hits) with no eligible repository; DbtDag query read to its end (30 hits), hainguyenle89/airflow-dags at hit 13 the only eligible one. Later hits were not evaluated. Repository sizes were checked before fetching; all were under 200 MB and none is a fork.
conventions: Task built by a helper in the same file: line is the operator call inside the helper, lines holds the helper's call site.
Task built by a helper in another file: file is the DAG file and line the helper's call site; the helper's location is in reason.
Custom operators are named by their own class; reason says which standard operator they use.
command_index counts every dbt command in the string, in-scope or not.
Selected models for dbt test also count a model that is only the 'to' target of a relationships test, because that test depends on it; disabled tests do not count.
dbt test has empty other_nodes, even when seeds or snapshots have tests.
Cosmos units have task_id null; other_nodes holds the seeds and snapshots they select.
When one dag_id and task appear in several files, id carries a @ suffix to stay unique.

Model sets were worked out by applying dbt's selection rules with a small script of the labeller's own that reads project text, then checked by eye. It is not the scanner, and nothing from the repositories was executed.

Fresh corpus: model sets were worked out by hand from each project's own text (dbt_project.yml, .sql files and their ref()/source() calls, YAML properties), applying dbt's selection rules, then checked with a small script of the labeller's own that confirms every listed file, line, project, model and seed exists. Nothing from the repositories was executed; a dbt library committed inside one repository's virtualenv was read only as text to confirm how dbt parses YAML in test-paths and applies --exclude to tests.
A dbt project at the repository root has project_path '.'.

dbt_projects lists the repository's own dbt projects; dbt_project.yml files inside a committed virtualenv's site-packages or inside dbt_packages belong to libraries or installed packages and are not listed.
A task inside a plain Airflow TaskGroup has the task_id Airflow gives it, prefixed with the group id (group.task); group_id stays null, as it is only used for Cosmos task groups.

Tasks generated in a loop from a committed target/manifest.json are one link per generated task, all with the same file and line; they are resolved when the committed manifest matches the project's sources.
When the operator carries no dbt command and the image entrypoint script runs dbt, command_index counts the dbt commands in that script in text order, including any on branches not taken.
A command given without the dbt executable, because the image entrypoint is dbt, and a command run through the dbt-ol (OpenLineage) wrapper are labelled with the dbt command they run.
Operators other than the five searched for (an SSHOperator running dbt on another host, for example) are labelled like any other task, with the project that host holds.
A task built only when an environment variable allows it is still labelled; the condition is in reason.
